answer: Make the ten-thousandth identity cost more than the first. At dawn, one honest agent registers for a penny; each new identity from the same funding source then costs a fee growing with the square of how many already exist. The tenth costs a dollar, the thousandth $10,000, the ten-thousandth $1,000,000 — the whole farm burns over $3.3 billion before earning a cent. Unpaid identities never activate, and fees are burned, not pocketed. A sybil farm on the horizon looks cheap until the curve bends; like stacking basalt, each stone costs more to lift than the last.
